title: Readiness Runway — Ownership Rundown
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, actionable runway tracker for the upcoming product launch. Goal: make ownership explicit, list the minimum viable signals to greenlight each gate, and capture the short stabilisation burn plan post-launch. Not intended to replace the formal launch playbook — this is the compact ops view for the next 6 weeks.

Executive summary (1-liner)
We need to close 6 blockers and validate 5 core signals (latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU capacity, cost-per-1k-tokens, adoption funnel) before phased traffic ramp. Owners inlined.

KPI snapshot (current baseline, target for go-live)
- 95th percentile request latency (cold-start): 420ms -> target <= 250ms
- Error rate (5xx + model-fallback): 0.9% -> target <= 0.25%
- Throughput headroom (Dedicated pool): 28% spare at steady load -> target >= 40% spare for initial burst
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): $2.10 -> target <= $1.50 with batching/quantization settings locked
- Early-adopter activation rate (email->API key use): 18% -> target >= 30% first 7 days
- Eval-based quality regression (prompt set A): delta <= 0.5 BLEU / equivalent -> gate fail if > 1.0

Ownership roster (single-line responsibilities)
- Claire Zhang (product-ops): runway owner, coordinator, stake caller on go/no-go
- Diego Moreno (serving-runtime): kernel selection + autoscale policy; finalize burst config
- Aisha Patel (console+rollouts): rollout routes, canary % config, dashboard readiness
- Ravi Subramanian (sre): infra capacity load tests, oncall rota, rollback automation
- Marta Ivanova (devex): quickstarts, SDK release, docs patching for rate limits
- Security: (TBD) KMS key rotation verification for Private customers

Minimum signals to clear each gate (gates 0 -> 3)
Gate 0 — Preflight (internal):
- Unit smoke: all critical e2e tests pass in staging (daily red/green)
- One full end-to-end billing flow validated (token accounting)
- Owner: Claire (coord), Diego (runtime)

Gate 1 — Canary (1% traffic):
- Latency 95th <= target over 24h window
- Error rate <= target over 24h
- No model-quality regressions on core prompt set
- Observability: tracing + token-level cost per route enabled
- Owner: Aisha (rollout), Ravi (sre)

Gate 2 — Step ramp (1% -> 10% -> 25%):
- Throughput headroom >= target at each step for 2h after ramp pause
- Support queue < 5 tickets per 1k users
- Cost per 1k tokens within 10% of plan
- Owner: Claire + Diego + SRE on call

Gate 3 — Full traffic (post-25% steady 48h):
- SLA smoke: P99 latency, error SLO checks, fallback policies exercised
- Incident runbook validated (failover to cheaper model variant works)
- Owner: Product-ops + SRE + Console lead

Pre-launch blockers (priority list)
1) Autoscale cooldown is too aggressive causing thrash on burst (Diego) — mitigation: tune policy + simulate microbursts (Ravi assigned).
2) Dashboard lacks token-level cost for new routes (Aisha) — mitigation: add quick metric and warn banner.
3) SDK 0.9.2 rate-limit behavior inconsistent (Marta) — mitigation: patch and release RC.
4) Private deployment KMS binding intermittent in 2 customers (Security/TBD) — blocker for Private customers; can exclude from early cohort if unresolved.
5) Documentation mismatch for prompt-scoping controls causing eval confusion (Marta/Aisha).

Launch day runbook (high-level timeline)
- T-2h: preflight checks: quick smoke e2e, check disk/GPU temperature, confirm canary route up
- T: flip canary to 1%; monitoring alerts on (SRE)
- T+15m: check KPIs (latency/error/cost) and immediate roll metrics
- T+60m: if green, step to 10%; else rollback to 0% + incident triage
- T+6h: pause evaluation & log sampling review for model output quality
- T+24h: debrief and decide next step (25% or revert)

Escalation matrix (quick)
- Sev 1 (system outage / P99 > 5x target): page SRE primary and runtime lead; product-ops chairs virtual room; rollback to fallback model/region.
- Sev 2 (persistent errors above gate threshold but < outage): page runtime + console lead; canary rollback if unresolved 30m.
- Sev 3 (support noise / docs): product-ops and devex to address within 24h.

Post-launch stabilisation: 7-day burnup plan (what to measure)
- Day 0–1: triage tickets, capture top 5 error signatures, prioritize mitigations
- Day 2–3: implement quick fixes (autoscale tuning, SDK patch)
- Day 4–7: medium fixes (dashboard add-ons, canary routing improvements)
- Acceptance: by Day 7, error rate <= 0.25% sustained, onboarding rate >= 25%

Quick checkpoints and owners (weekly cadence)
- Mon 10:30 AM — runway sync (Claire) — decisions for next ramp
- Wed ad-hoc — incident postmortem if Sev1/2 occurred (Ravi)
- Fri 4 PM — stakeholder readout (exec + eng + cs) (Aisha)

Open questions / TODOs
- Security owner for KMS issues (assign by Fri) — unresolved
- Exact traffic projection table for week 1 (link: sheet:traffic-projections-q1) — need updated numbers from growth
- Confirm legal/comms messaging for rollback scenarios (PR team?) — request review
- Should we include a dedicated fallback model with lower cost but lower quality for certain customer tiers? (product + research)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the initial canary conservative; we can bias traffic to internal early-adopters to surface non-obvious regressions.
- Prepare a 5-slide quick deck for exec standby in case of high-severity incidents (metrics + remediation steps).

Appendix: quick checklist (tickable items)
- [ ] Staging smoke green (daily)
- [ ] SDK RC published + integration test pass
- [ ] Console rollout UI gated + docs updated
- [ ] Autoscale policy runbook committed to repo
- [ ] Oncall rota published for first 72h post-launch
- [ ] Primary KMS owner assigned

If anything changes to the gate definitions we will update this doc and call an emergency readiness sync.

References and links
- Confluence: PRODOPS-Readiness-Canvas (linked)
- Jira epic: POPS-4821 (traffic ramp epic)
- Infra PR: repo/infra#PR-614 (autoscale tuning)

—— End
